newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel office rules against Lufthansa. [CORRECTED 10:28 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German cartel office rules against Lufthansa. [CORRECTED 10:28 GMT]

text.p: The German cartel office said on Monday an investigation into Lufthansa AG had concluded the German national airline was overcharging for tickets on flights between Frankfurt and Berlin.
(Corrects to reflect that investigation completed and a ruling has been issued).
Lufthansa said it would fight the ruling in court.
The cartel office in January had issued a caution to Lufthansa for charging excessive prices on the route and had given the airline a month to respond.

A cartel office spokesman said the ruling would allow Lufthansa to charge only 10 marks more for a one-way ticket on the Berlin-Frankfurt route as it does on the Munich-Berlin route, where Lufthansa faces competition from Deutsche BA.

Lufthansa has defended the prices it charges on the Frankfurt-Berlin route, saying they were necessary to cover costs. A roundtrip business-class ticket between Frankfurt and Berlin costs about 160 marks more than on the Berlin-Munich route.
Lufthansa has said it was contemplating whether to pull out of the Berlin-Frankfurt route and to find a partner airline to operate the service.
